definition: Whether the algorithm learns only from data generated by the current policy (PPO, GRPO: fresher signal, more expensive) or can reuse data from older or different policies (Q-learning, offline RL: sample-efficient, riskier).
details: Whether the algorithm learns only from data generated by the current policy (PPO, GRPO: fresher signal, more expensive) or can reuse data from older or different policies (Q-learning, offline RL: sample-efficient, riskier).

explainer.lead: On-policy versus off-policy describes whether an algorithm learns only from data generated by the current policy or can reuse data from older or different policies. The choice trades fresher signal against sample efficiency.

tiers.eli5: On-policy is like practising with today's playbook only; off-policy is like also studying recordings of last season's games.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose on-policy methods such as PPO and GRPO for fresher signal at higher cost, and off-policy methods such as Q-learning and offline RL for sample efficiency, accepting more risk.
tiers.paperLevel: On-policy algorithms (PPO, GRPO) learn from data of the current policy, giving fresher signal at greater expense; off-policy algorithms (Q-learning, offline RL) reuse data from older or different policies, gaining sample efficiency at greater risk.

explainer.example: A team with a costly simulator trains with PPO rather than reusing old logs, trading expense for data that matches the current policy.
